name: Atom
description: Atom syndication format and publishing protocol

rfc4287.title: The Atom Syndication Format
rfc4287.abstract: This document specifies Atom, an XML-based Web content and metadata syndication format. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc4685.title: Atom Threading Extensions
rfc4685.abstract: This memo presents a mechanism that allows feeds publishers to express threaded discussions within the Atom Syndication Format. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc4946.title: Atom License Extension
rfc4946.abstract: This memo defines an extension to the Atom Syndication Format for describing licenses associated with Atom feeds and entries.  This memo defines an Experimental Protocol for the Internet community.

rfc5005.title: Feed Paging and Archiving
rfc5005.abstract: This specification defines three types of syndicated Web feeds that enable publication of entries across one or more feed documents.  This includes "paged" feeds for piecemeal access, "archived" feeds that allow reconstruction of the feed's contents, and feeds that are explicitly "complete". [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc5023.title: The Atom Publishing Protocol
rfc5023.abstract: The Atom Publishing Protocol (AtomPub) is an application-level protocol for publishing and editing Web resources.  The protocol is based on HTTP transfer of Atom-formatted representations.  The Atom format is documented in the Atom Syndication Format. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc6721.title: The Atom "deleted-entry" Element
rfc6721.abstract: This specification adds mechanisms to the Atom Syndication Format that publishers of Atom Feed and Entry documents can use to explicitly identify Atom entries that have been removed. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc8322.title: Resource-Oriented Lightweight Information Exchange (ROLIE)
rfc8322.abstract: This document defines a resource-oriented approach for security automation information publication, discovery, and sharing.  Using this approach, producers may publish, share, and exchange representations of software descriptors, security incidents, attack indicators, software vulnerabilities, configuration checklists, and other security automation information as web-addressable resources.  Furthermore, consumers and other stakeholders may access and search this security information as needed, establishing a rapid and on-demand information exchange network for restricted internal use or public access repositories.  This specification extends the Atom Publishing Protocol and Atom Syndication Format to transport and share security automation resource representations.
